amc8-2005-01.title: Undo the mistake
amc8-2005-01.body:
Doubling gave $60$, so the number is $60 \div 2 = 30$. Halving it gives $30 \div 2 = 15$.

**Answer: (B) 15**

amc8-2005-01.title: Compare the two results
amc8-2005-01.body:
Dividing by $2$ instead of multiplying by $2$ gives a result $4$ times smaller: $60 \div 4 = 15$.

**Answer: (B) 15**

amc8-2005-02.title: Per folder
amc8-2005-02.body:
Each folder would be $20\%$ of $\$2.50$, i.e. $\$0.50$, cheaper. Five folders: $5 \times \$0.50 = \$2.50$.

**Answer: (C) \$2.50**

amc8-2005-03.title: Reflect each black square
amc8-2005-03.body:
Reflecting across diagonal $BD$ swaps rows and columns. Check each black square's mirror image:
- the square in the top-right corner (next to $B$) lies on the diagonal and is its own mirror image;
- each of the other four black squares has a white mirror image.

So $4$ more squares must be colored: the minimum is $4$.

**Answer: (D) 4**

amc8-2005-04.title: Perimeter, side, area
amc8-2005-04.body:
Triangle perimeter: $6.1 + 8.2 + 9.7 = 24$ cm. The square's side is $24 \div 4 = 6$ cm, so its area is $36$ cm².

**Answer: (C) 36**

amc8-2005-05.title: Use big packs first
amc8-2005-05.body:
Use as many 24-packs as possible: three give $72$, leaving $18 = 12 + 6$. Total $3 + 1 + 1 = 5$ packs.

Four packs can't work: four 24-packs give $96$, and with at most three 24-packs, four packs hold at most $72 + 12 = 84 < 90$. So $5$ is the minimum.

**Answer: (B) 5**

amc8-2005-06.title: Compare digit by digit
amc8-2005-06.body:
Write $2.005 = 2.0050$. Then $2.00d5 > 2.0050$ means $\overline{d5} > 50$, i.e. $d \ge 5$. The digits $5, 6, 7, 8, 9$ work: $5$ values.

**Answer: (C) 5**

amc8-2005-07.title: Right triangle
amc8-2005-07.body:
In total he went $1$ mile south and $\frac34$ mile east. The direct distance is $\sqrt{1^2 + (3/4)^2} = \sqrt{\frac{25}{16}} = \frac54 = 1\frac14$ miles.

**Answer: (B) $1\tfrac14$**

amc8-2005-07.title: Scale a 3-4-5 triangle
amc8-2005-07.body:
The legs $\frac34$ and $1 = \frac44$ are $3$ and $4$ quarter-miles, so the hypotenuse is $5$ quarter-miles: $1\frac14$ miles.

**Answer: (B) $1\tfrac14$**

amc8-2005-08.title: Parity rules
amc8-2005-08.body:
odd $\times$ odd $=$ odd and odd $+$ odd $=$ even.
- $m + 3n$: odd + odd = even.
- $3m - n$: odd − odd = even.
- $3m^2 + 3n^2$: odd + odd = even.
- $(nm + 3)^2$: $nm + 3$ is odd + odd = even, so its square is even.
- $3mn$: odd × odd × odd = odd. ✓

**Answer: (E) $3mn$**

amc8-2005-08.title: Try numbers
amc8-2005-08.body:
Take $m = n = 1$: the choices give $4, 2, 6, 16, 3$. Only $3mn$ is odd.

**Answer: (E) $3mn$**

amc8-2005-09.title: Equilateral triangle
amc8-2005-09.body:
In triangle $ACD$, $DA = DC = 17$ and the angle between them is $60^\circ$. An isosceles triangle with a $60^\circ$ apex angle has base angles $\frac{180^\circ - 60^\circ}{2} = 60^\circ$ too, so it is equilateral and $AC = 17$.

**Answer: (D) 17**

amc8-2005-10.title: Same distance, 3 times as fast
amc8-2005-10.body:
The second half is the same distance as the first, run 3 times as fast, so it takes $6 \div 3 = 2$ minutes. Total $6 + 2 = 8$ minutes.

**Answer: (D) 8**

amc8-2005-11.title: Order doesn't matter
amc8-2005-11.body:
Jack computes $90 \times 1.06 \times 0.8$ and Jill computes $90 \times 0.8 \times 1.06$. Multiplication can be done in any order, so the totals are equal and the difference is \$0.

**Answer: (C) \$0**

amc8-2005-12.title: Use the middle day
amc8-2005-12.body:
The five amounts go up by $6$ each day, so they are evenly spaced and the May 3 amount is the average: $100 \div 5 = 20$. Then May 4: $26$, May 5: $32$.

**Answer: (D) 32**

amc8-2005-13.title: Missing rectangle
amc8-2005-13.body:
Complete the polygon to an $8 \times 9$ rectangle (area $72$). The missing corner rectangle has area $72 - 52 = 20$. Its sides are $DE$ and $EF$. Vertically, $DE = BC - FA = 9 - 5 = 4$, so $EF = 20 \div 4 = 5$. Then $DE + EF = 4 + 5 = 9$.

**Answer: (C) 9**

amc8-2005-13.title: Split into two rectangles
amc8-2005-13.body:
Cut horizontally through $F$: the top rectangle is $8 \times 5 = 40$, so the bottom rectangle (right part) has area $52 - 40 = 12$ and height $9 - 5 = 4$, so its width $CD = 3$. Then $EF = 8 - 3 = 5$, $DE = 4$, sum $9$.

**Answer: (C) 9**

amc8-2005-14.title: Count each type of game
amc8-2005-14.body:
In one division, $\binom62 = 15$ pairs each play twice: $30$ games. Two divisions: $60$. Every one of the $6 \times 6 = 36$ cross-division pairs plays once: $36$. Total $60 + 36 = 96$.

**Answer: (B) 96**

amc8-2005-14.title: Count per team, then halve
amc8-2005-14.body:
Each team plays $5 \times 2 + 6 = 16$ games. $12 \times 16 = 192$ counts every game twice, so there are $96$ games.

**Answer: (B) 96**

amc8-2005-15.title: List by the equal sides
amc8-2005-15.body:
Let the sides be $a, a, b$ with $2a + b = 23$. The triangle inequality needs $b < 2a$, so $23 - 2a < 2a$, $a > 5.75$, i.e. $a \ge 6$. Also $b \ge 1$ means $a \le 11$. So $a = 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11$ (with $b = 11, 9, 7, 5, 3, 1$): $6$ triangles. (None is counted twice, since $b$ is odd and $a = b$ would need $3a = 23$.)

**Answer: (C) 6**

amc8-2005-16.title: Worst case
amc8-2005-16.body:
With $12$ socks the Martian could have exactly $4$ of each color and still not have $5$ of one color. The $13$th sock must make $5$ of some color. So $13$.

**Answer: (D) 13**

amc8-2005-17.title: Steepest line from the origin
amc8-2005-17.body:
Average speed is distance ÷ time, which is the slope of the line from $O$ to the student's point. Evelyn's point is high up (large distance) and far to the left (small time), so her line is the steepest: she has the greatest average speed.

**Answer: (E) Evelyn**

amc8-2005-18.title: First and last multiples
amc8-2005-18.body:
The smallest three-digit multiple of $13$ is $104 = 13 \times 8$, and the largest is $988 = 13 \times 76$. So the multiples are $13 \times 8$ through $13 \times 76$: $76 - 8 + 1 = 69$ numbers.

**Answer: (C) 69**

amc8-2005-18.title: Count up to 999
amc8-2005-18.body:
$\lfloor 999/13 \rfloor = 76$ multiples are at most $999$, and $\lfloor 99/13 \rfloor = 7$ of them are at most $99$. So $76 - 7 = 69$.

**Answer: (C) 69**

amc8-2005-19.title: Pythagorean triples
amc8-2005-19.body:
Drop heights of $24$ from $B$ and $C$. On the left, $30^2 - 24^2 = 324$, so $AE = 18$. On the right, $25^2 - 24^2 = 49$, so that piece is $7$. The bottom base is $18 + 50 + 7 = 75$.

Perimeter: $30 + 50 + 25 + 75 = 180$.

**Answer: (A) 180**

amc8-2005-20.title: Bob in clockwise terms
amc8-2005-20.body:
Moving $9$ points counterclockwise on a $12$-point circle is the same as moving $3$ points clockwise. So each turn Alice gains $5 - 3 = 2$ points on Bob. They meet when Alice is a full $12$ points ahead: $12 \div 2 = 6$ turns.

**Answer: (A) 6**

amc8-2005-20.title: Track positions
amc8-2005-20.body:
After $t$ turns Alice is at $5t$ and Bob at $-9t$ (mod $12$). They coincide when $14t$ is a multiple of $12$, i.e. $7t$ a multiple of $6$, so $t = 6$.

**Answer: (A) 6**

amc8-2005-21.title: Subtract the straight lines
amc8-2005-21.body:
There are $6$ dots in two rows of $3$. Choosing any $3$ dots: $\binom63 = 20$ ways. The only collinear triples are the two rows, so $20 - 2 = 18$ triangles.

**Answer: (C) 18**

amc8-2005-21.title: Two from one row
amc8-2005-21.body:
A triangle uses $2$ dots from one row and $1$ from the other: $\binom32 \cdot 3 = 9$ for each choice of row, $18$ in all.

**Answer: (C) 18**

amc8-2005-22.title: Pick convenient numbers
amc8-2005-22.body:
Say small costs \$1.00 and holds $10$ oz.
- Large holds $20$ oz; medium holds $20\%$ less: $16$ oz.
- Medium costs $50\%$ more than small: \$1.50; large costs $30\%$ more than medium: \$1.95.

Cost per ounce: S $10$¢, M $\frac{150}{16} \approx 9.4$¢, L $\frac{195}{20} = 9.75$¢. Best to worst: M, L, S.

**Answer: (E) MLS**

amc8-2005-23.title: Find the radius
amc8-2005-23.body:
Semicircle area $\frac12 \pi r^2 = 2\pi$ gives $r = 2$. The radii to the tangent points are perpendicular to the legs, so they form a $2 \times 2$ square with corner $C$. By symmetry $O$ is the midpoint of $AB$, and each leg is twice the square's side: $AC = BC = 4$. Area $= \frac12 \cdot 4 \cdot 4 = 8$.

**Answer: (B) 8**

amc8-2005-23.title: Reflect into a square
amc8-2005-23.body:
Reflect the triangle across $AB$: you get a square with the full circle (radius $2$) inscribed, so its side is $4$ and area $16$. The triangle is half: $8$.

**Answer: (B) 8**

amc8-2005-24.title: Work backwards
amc8-2005-24.body:
Going backwards, halve when the number is even (that's always the best), and subtract $1$ when it's odd:
$200 \to 100 \to 50 \to 25 \to 24 \to 12 \to 6 \to 3 \to 2 \to 1$.
That's $9$ keystrokes: $1 \xrightarrow{+1} 2 \xrightarrow{+1} 3 \xrightarrow{\times2} 6 \to 12 \to 24 \xrightarrow{+1} 25 \xrightarrow{\times2} 50 \to 100 \to 200$.

**Answer: (B) 9**

amc8-2005-24.title: Binary view
amc8-2005-24.body:
$200 = 11001000_2$. Starting from $1$, each $\times2$ adds a binary digit and each $+1$ turns a final $0$ into $1$. We need $7$ doublings (to get $8$ binary digits) and $2$ extra $+1$'s for the other two $1$ digits: $9$ keystrokes.

**Answer: (B) 9**

amc8-2005-25.title: Equal leftovers mean equal areas
amc8-2005-25.body:
Let $X$ be the overlap of circle and square. The circle's area is $X + (\text{circle outside square})$ and the square's area is $X + (\text{square outside circle})$. These two leftover areas are equal, so the circle and the square have the same area: $\pi r^2 = 4$, $r = \frac{2}{\sqrt\pi}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}}$**
